stories.headline: Emergency declared at South Carolina's Savannah River nuclear site after a fire breaks out at its national lab
stories.summary: The Savannah River Site near Aiken, South Carolina, declared a Site Area Emergency at 5:39 p.m. Wednesday after a fire broke out at the Savannah River National Laboratory, according to the Department of Energy. The fire was put out and one employee was taken to a hospital with minor injuries, and a DOE spokesperson said no radiological contamination has been reported. As a precaution, site entrances were barricaded to incoming traffic, rail, river and air traffic near the site was restricted, and workers in affected areas who are not part of the response were told to shelter in place. Residents were advised to follow local radio and TV for instructions. The sprawling DOE complex, built in the 1950s to make tritium and plutonium for nuclear weapons, still manages nuclear materials and radioactive waste for the weapons program.

stories.headline: Minnesota prosecutor charges James O'Keefe and Cam Higby with felonies over their undercover polling-place video
stories.summary: Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty on Wednesday charged journalist James O'Keefe, 42, and conservative activist Cam Higby, 26, with felony unlawful voting and identity theft, each punishable by up to five years in prison. The charges stem from an August video O'Keefe posted of the pair entering Minneapolis polling places on primary day in Islamic garb, using fake accents and hidden cameras, to draw attention to Minnesota's voter-vouching law, which lets one registered voter vouch for the residency of up to eight recently moved voters. Prosecutors say O'Keefe "intentionally misrepresented their identities in applying for ballots," though neither complaint alleges they actually cast a vote. Moriarty, a progressive prosecutor elected in 2022, said the charges have nothing to do with the men's politics or the disguises, while supporters call it retaliation for exposing an election-security loophole days before the Nov. 3 midterms.

stories.headline: Hacker steals records on more than 41,000 DHS employees, including thousands of ICE and CBP agents
stories.summary: A hacker calling itself "Department of Peace" stole the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses and office locations of more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, according to TechCrunch and Wired. About 21,000 of the records belong to Customs and Border Protection staff and nearly 7,000 to ICE, with others from CISA, USCIS and Homeland Security Investigations. The hacker reportedly got in through Okta, the identity and login service DHS uses, and said "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The data, dubbed "Icepick," was passed to the leak site DDoSecrets and also ties DHS units to surveillance tools such as the Mobile Fortify facial recognition app and PenLink phone-data software. It comes weeks after a similar theft of FBI employee and applicant data, and as DHS has been trying to shield the identities of agents carrying out immigration raids. DHS did not immediately comment.

stories.headline: Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want a trade out of New York, but admits he's frustrated as the 2-5 Jets keep losing
stories.summary: Jets star receiver Garrett Wilson shot down trade chatter on Wednesday, saying "I want to be here, man... I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful." Wilson had just two catches for 26 yards on three targets in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the previously winless Dolphins, and TV cameras caught him shouting on the sideline toward Geno Smith and passing-game coordinator Seth Ryan. He said his frustration comes from wanting to win, not from wanting the ball, and that he has not asked to be traded. Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million extension in 2025, still leads the team with 37 catches for 444 yards and three touchdowns, but has never had a winning season since New York drafted him in 2022. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Jets host Kirk Cousins and the Raiders on Sunday.

stories.headline: Putin calls Elon Musk 'a real genius' and says Moscow is in contact with him on space, days after Ukraine's Starshield came back
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk on Wednesday during an exhibition visit at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, saying "Elon Musk is a genius, a real genius" as Russia scrambles to build its own answer to Starlink. Putin said that "despite all political issues" Moscow keeps in contact with its "U.S. partners, including Mr. Musk" on space matters, and that Roscosmos and other companies are working together. The remarks came less than a week after Ukraine restored full-speed use of commercial Starlink terminals and the military Starshield version following a restriction that began Oct. 14 and capped terminal speeds in a way that hampered Ukrainian drone interceptors. Musk has accused Ukraine of breaking the terms of service by using commercial terminals for offensive drone strikes, which Kyiv denies; neither Musk nor the Trump administration has claimed responsibility for the throttling.

stories.headline: RFK Jr.'s HHS will let small compounding pharmacies make six popular wellness peptides the FDA never approved
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services says it will use "enforcement discretion" for six peptides, in effect letting small 503A compounding pharmacies make them even though the FDA has not approved them. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has long backed wider access and says he has used some peptides himself. Peptides, short chains of amino acids promoted by wellness influencers for many uses, have been sold on a gray market as "research-use-only" products often sourced from overseas, and HHS argues compounding is a safer option. An FDA advisory panel voted in July to allow compounding of the six, though the agency's own scientists recommended against it. Pharmacists warn the small shops covered by the policy won't be able to meet demand, and the larger 503B outsourcing facilities are excluded. Consumer groups such as Public Citizen say the move puts patients at risk and skipped normal rulemaking.

stories.headline: Florida man charged with murder 15 years after his ex-fiancée vanished hours after their 'People's Court' taping
stories.summary: Orlando police have charged Dale Smith Jr., 55, with second-degree murder in the 2011 disappearance of Michelle Parker, his ex-fiancée and the mother of his twins, whose body has never been found. Court documents unsealed Tuesday say a fresh look at cellphone data and texts broke the case. On Nov. 17, 2011, the two taped an episode of "The People's Court" over a $5,000 engagement ring she allegedly threw off a balcony; the judge told them to split the cost. Smith said Parker dropped off the kids and left within 10 minutes, but surveillance video showed her Hummer at his home for at least an hour, and both of their phones then left together heading west, away from the mall her phone later texted that she was at. Investigators note Smith never called or messaged her again after that day. He was arrested Oct. 14, and police say he has a history of domestic violence.

stories.headline: iPhone Duo could take nearly 30% of the foldable phone market in 2027, TrendForce says after a strong first week
stories.summary: With the iPhone Duo shipping for almost a week, market researcher TrendForce reiterated its forecast that Apple will ship about 5 million of its first foldable by the end of 2026, about 24.8% of the segment, and said Apple should reach 29.8% of the global foldable smartphone market in 2027. TrendForce expects the overall foldable market to grow 16.3% next year to 23.5 million units after nearly flat 2026, when Android brands' foldable shipments are expected to drop by more than 20%. It credits Apple's ability to integrate its chips, operating system and developer ecosystem, and says better app support and hardware reliability could shift foldable competition from novel form factors toward multitasking. If the forecast holds, Apple would rank second in 2027 behind Samsung, whose share is seen slipping from 35.1% to 31.9%, and ahead of Huawei, projected to fall from 24.8% to 21.3%.

stories.headline: Al Jourgensen sets Ministry's final concert for Oct. 30, 2027 at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles
stories.summary: Industrial-metal pioneer Al Jourgensen says Ministry will play its last show on Oct. 30, 2027, exactly one year after the release of its 17th and final album, "Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)," with a blowout concert at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. He told interviewer Lyndsey Parker the night will be "a procession" of musicians Ministry influenced coming up to jam and say goodbye, and joked that comedian Bill Burr will helicopter him home before fans are even let backstage. The final album, out this Friday, includes one last collaboration with longtime bandmate Paul Barker on its closing track, "We're Still Here." Since 1981 Ministry has gone from 1983's synth-pop "With Sympathy" to the industrial assault of "The Land Of Rape And Honey" and 1992's "Psalm 69," and Jourgensen says he is happy to call it a career.

stories.headline: US sends recon Marines to the Baltic Sea to help NATO guard undersea cables against Russian sabotage
stories.summary: About four dozen Marines from Camp Lejeune's 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion and II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group are deploying to the Baltic Sea to join Finnish forces in NATO's Baltic Sentry operation, Task & Purpose reported. They will use surveillance drones and coastal sensors to watch over undersea internet cables and energy pipelines that run between Russia and the EU. Since the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions there have been more than half a dozen attempted attacks on Baltic cables and pipelines. Europe has more undersea cables than anywhere else, and these lines carry most of the world's internet traffic and an estimated $10 trillion in financial transactions a day. The Marine Corps called the mission a defensive move meant to show the alliance can deter and defeat any threat to the region.

stories.headline: Woman in a burqa is escorted out of a Florida county meeting after playing the Islamic call to prayer at the podium
stories.summary: During public comment at a Pinellas County Board of County Commissioners meeting on Tuesday, a woman covered head to toe in black walked to the podium and, instead of speaking, played a recording of the Islamic call to prayer for nearly a minute. Chairman Dave Eggers stopped her, saying county rules require speakers to make spoken comments rather than play recordings, and a sheriff's deputy escorted her out of the room and the building when she refused, sparking shouting in the audience. It was not clear whether it was a protest or a prank. The meeting's public comment period was dominated by residents objecting to the board's 4-3 vote on Oct. 13 to approve a land-use change for the expansion of the Masjid Al Rahman mosque, which county documents described as a "community assembly facility."

stories.headline: It's official: Apple unveils its first touchscreen Mac, an OLED MacBook Pro starting at $2,899
stories.summary: Apple announced a new high-end MacBook Pro at its "Pro and tell" launch Wednesday, in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes starting at $2,899 and $3,399. Its new PROLED XDR display uses tandem OLED with up to 2,000 nits of brightness and 120Hz ProMotion, and it is the first Mac with a touchscreen: the touch sensor is built into the panel, a new hinge keeps the screen steady when you tap it, and macOS translates touches into clicks so existing apps work right away. The notch is replaced by a small Dynamic Island for Spotlight, Live Activities and Siri, bezels are thinner, the 14-inch weighs three pounds, and the glowing Apple logo is back on the lid for the first time in about 10 years. It uses the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips with up to 128GB of memory and up to 16TB of storage, plus three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SD slot and MagSafe. Pre-orders are open now, and it launches Friday, Nov. 6, alongside the existing mini-LED models and a new M6 14-inch MacBook Pro.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates steady under Warsh despite 3.7% inflation, and plans to cut back on rate-setting meetings
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, its last meeting before the midterm elections, after raising rates in September for the first time in more than three years. Inflation has kept climbing since then, with consumer prices up 3.7% from a year earlier in September, driven partly by an energy-price spike tied to the war with Iran, and investors widely expect a hike in December. Two policymakers, Fed governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, voted to raise rates a quarter point now. Mortgage rates hit a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month. After the decision, Chairman Kevin Warsh announced that starting next fall, one of the Fed's eight yearly meetings will be devoted to big-picture strategy instead of a rate vote, rising to two in 2028, ending a calendar the Fed has followed since 1981, NBC News reported.

stories.headline: Dolores Huerta, United Farm Workers co-founder who coined 'Sí, se puede,' dies at 96
stories.summary: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve conditions for workers in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields, died Wednesday at her home, her family said through her Bakersfield, California-based foundation. She was 96. Huerta coined the slogan "Sí, se puede!" ("Yes, it can be done"), which became a widespread rallying cry, and she kept marching and speaking around the country well into her 90s. President Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012 and joked that he had borrowed her slogan for his 2008 campaign. Earlier this year she revealed that she had been sexually abused in the 1960s by the movement's other co-founder, César Chavez, leading to the birth of two children, a secret she kept for 60 years because she feared it would unravel the progress made for workers.

stories.headline: Chiefs sign Justin Tucker, out of the NFL since 2024, and Andy Reid defends the move: 'He's done his suspension'
stories.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs signed former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker, 37, to their practice squad Wednesday as competition for Harrison Butker, who has missed five of his 16 field-goal attempts this season. Tucker hasn't played since the 2024 season. In early 2025, 16 massage therapists accused him of inappropriate sexual behavior during sessions between 2012 and 2016, which he denied, and the NFL suspended him for the first 10 weeks of the 2025 season; no team signed him afterward, though he worked out for the Dolphins earlier this year. Asked what message the signing sends to female fans, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said, "He's done his suspension. Took care of his business there. I'll leave it at that," adding that the team "talked to a lot of people" and did its homework first.

stories.headline: Rubin Observatory finds a possible new dwarf planet beyond Pluto, the biggest such find in 20 years
stories.summary: Just four months into its 10-year sky survey, the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile has turned up an icy world orbiting beyond Pluto that could be the solar system's sixth recognized dwarf planet. Provisionally named 2026 ED138, it is roughly 1,000 kilometers (621 miles) across, making it the largest trans-Neptunian object discovered in about 20 years and one of the biggest and brightest ever found in that region. "Finding an object this big is something that happens maybe once in a generation," said Mario Jurić of the University of Washington, who leads Rubin's solar system team. Harvard-Smithsonian astrophysicist Matthew Holman spotted it with search code that links billions of detections of moving objects, and said his first reaction was "excited disbelief." Rubin, which has the largest digital camera ever built for astronomy, found it while the telescope was still being commissioned.

stories.headline: Metallica and the Red Cross set a three-day blood drive at Mohegan Sun ahead of the band's Connecticut shows
stories.summary: Metallica and the American Red Cross are teaming up again for a blood drive ahead of the band's upcoming concerts at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, which celebrate the arena's 25th anniversary. Donors of all blood types, especially type O, can give in Mohegan Sun's Uncas Ballroom on Wednesday, Nov. 18, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Friday, Nov. 20, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; and Saturday, Nov. 21, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. Everyone who donates gets an exclusive Red Cross x Metallica T-shirt while supplies last. Appointments can be booked at rcblood.org/BleedMetallica, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or through the Blood Donor App. Mohegan Sun says the band's blood drive campaign has collected tens of thousands of donations worldwide since it began last year.

stories.headline: VW's EV battery-fire recall grows past 85,000 vehicles as Audi Q4 e-tron owners are told to stop charging at 80%
stories.summary: Volkswagen's battery recall now covers 85,402 electric vehicles worldwide after the company added 12,734 Audi Q4 e-tron and Q4 Sportback e-tron SUVs, including 9,048 model-year 2024 and 2025 vehicles in the U.S. The problem is a risk that the battery overheats and catches fire when charged above 80% under certain conditions; Volkswagen's filing says some charging profiles combined with a high state of charge "may trigger thermal propagation," and the root cause is still unknown. Earlier this month VW recalled 22,524 ID.4 SUVs from model years 2023 to 2026 in the U.S., and German regulators list affected ID. Buzz, ID.3, ID.4, ID.7 and Cupra Born models built since 2022. Owners are being told to limit charging to 80%, and VW is pushing a temporary setting that caps it automatically unless owners opted out.

stories.headline: Trumbull weekend: Halloween dance party and trick-or-treating at Trumbull Mall on Friday night
stories.summary: Trumbull Mall is throwing a costume party the night before Halloween, with a DJ, music, games, crafts and trick-or-treating for the whole family on Friday evening, Oct. 30. Patch's weekend guide for Trumbull suggests bringing the kids in costume for a Halloween warm-up the night before the holiday.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: early voting’s final week at the library, a Town Hall Halloween parade for preschoolers, and a Hillcrest update
stories.summary: Early voting runs its final week in the Trumbull Library Community Room, 33 Quality St., from Monday, Oct. 26, through Sunday, Nov. 1. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 10 and 11:30 a.m., Town Hall staff host a costume parade and trick-or-treating past decorated office doors for registered Trumbull kids ages 0 to 5. Each session is limited to 20 children. That evening the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets project updates and the EMS Commission reviews vehicles, staffing and plans for Trumbull EMS’s 50th anniversary. The Conservation Commission meets Wednesday on tree rules and a spring 2027 tree giveaway.
